mission: Sleeping nook, night cycle. Ben strips his lightsaber to component parts to free his hands while his thoughts work. He types the full report to Luke — fortress, survivors, wound, Veraine. He reads it through twice. He deletes it with a single keystroke. Not because it is wrong. Because he does not trust the Order to respond correctly. The ghost file stays in memory; he does not clear it.
why_now: Torin's observation in the galley needs its private answer. The chapter cannot end with the observation hanging in the air; it ends with Ben choosing, one more day, to do the thing Torin just named.
conflict: Ben honestly knows he should tell Luke everything. He also honestly believes the Order would mishandle the response. The scene holds both truths without choosing between them in any way Ben can live with.
turning_point: Ben deletes the report with a single keystroke and does not clear the ghost file. Part of him knows he will need proof later that he tried. That part is not yet the loudest part.
opening_hook: Ben strips his lightsaber to component parts on the sleeping nook's fold-down shelf — a mindless maintenance ritual that frees his hands while his thoughts circle the comm field's blinking cursor
closing_hook: The deleted report leaves a ghost in Ben's datapad memory. He doesn't clear the ghost. Part of him knows he'll need proof later that he tried.
emotional_trajectory: Agonized deliberation -> attempted honesty -> rationalized secrecy

stakes.personal: Ben becoming, for a few hours, exactly what he is fighting against
stakes.interpersonal: His relationship with Luke deteriorating through silence
stakes.external: The Order remains ignorant while the crisis widens

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — Ben's sleeping nook, night cycle
sensory_details: Lightsaber components laid out in precise order — the familiar maintenance ritual grounding restless hands; the comm field's cursor blinking; the report's honest paragraphs on the datapad screen; the delete action; the ghost file's presence on the file index, not cleared; the wrongness a permanent background pressure, weather rather than event
action_beats: Ben strips his lightsaber to component parts and lays them on the sleeping nook's fold-down shelf
Ben types the full report — fortress, survivors, wound, Veraine — reads it through twice on the datapad
Ben deletes the report with a single keystroke and reassembles his lightsaber with hands that aren't quite steady
notes: SP4 reaches its deepest point inside Part 3. The irony is that Ben is doing what Gavran did, after Torin just told him so. The book refuses to underline the irony; the reader carries it. Use the lightsaber maintenance as physical architecture so the interiority has something to lean on — no more than half the scene in Ben's head, the ritual carrying the rest. Voice: Stover-interior-permitted in measured density; Zahn-restraint everywhere else. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, articulate 'I have become what I'm fighting' as an interior sentence. The delete keystroke is the statement; the unshredded ghost file is the residue of the part of him that knows. Rotate Force-wrongness metaphor here: weather/pressure (a migraine that will not break) — do not use handrail or flat-note.
